subject: HealthBridge deployment gating: isolation expectations & next steps
messages:
From: Emma Cole <emma.cole@healthbridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@healthbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today: deployment constraints and data handling

Thanks Rishi — good conversation today. Two quick clarifications from our side after the internal sync: 

- Primary constraint: anything touching PHI needs to remain under HealthBridge control (on-prem or dedicated VPC with customer key custody). Hosted multi-tenant API is a no-go for those flows.
- Secondary: non-PHI telemetry and analytics could be considered for hosted if we have strong pseudonymization and clear retention windows.

Can you confirm which Redwood deployment options (Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem) provide: 
1) Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for model inputs/outputs and KV cache? 
2) Separation of control-plane metadata from customer payloads (audit log visibility +/- access boundaries)? 
3) Audit evidence we can surface for procurement (SOC 2, rotation policies, network diagrams)?

I've attached a short spreadsheet with the set of security questions procurement wants answered before we can take this to legal. Also copying procurement so they can see scope/timeline constraints.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Cole
Director, Platform Security
HealthBridge

Attachment: healthbridge-soc2-request.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today: deployment constraints and data handling

Emma — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the procurement list. Short answers up front and then suggested next steps below.

At a glance: Hosted API = not suitable for PHI. Two viable patterns for PHI flows are: Dedicated capacity (single-tenant GPU pool with network restrictions) or Private deployment (VPC-connected control plane or fully on-prem bundle). Key tradeoffs summarized below:

- Customer-managed keys:
  - Dedicated: supports customer KMS/HSM integrations (you provide key material; Redwood can be configured to use customer CMKs for data-at-rest and model cache encryption).
  - Private (VPC / on-prem): full KMS/HSM control on the customer side — recommended if you must retain sole custody of keys.

- Control plane separation & audit:
  - Dedicated: control plane remains Redwood-managed but we can provide strict RBAC, audit log exports, and limited metadata retention policies. We can also disable certain telemetry collection on request.
  - Private: control plane can be in your VPC or on-prem; audit logs and metadata stay inside your network — best for regulated scenarios.

- Evidence for procurement: SOC 2 report + SOC bridge statement available for Hosted/Dedicated; for Private we provide architecture diagrams, runbooks, and can arrange an on-site SOC/engineering Q&A.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll upload a short comparison doc that maps your procurement questions to each deployment option (attachment).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Neha (our infra lead) and your SRE/security team to go over KMS/HSM specifics and network diagram requirements.
3) If Private is preferred, we'll produce a draft MOP (method of procedure) and a timeline for an on-prem or VPC private control plane engagement.

Would you be available for the deep-dive on Friday (Jun 12) or early next week?

Thanks,
Rishi
Sr. Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-deployment-comparison.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

Emma — adding a couple of technical clarifications from an infra standpoint: 

- KV cache: for Dedicated we can encrypt caches with customer keys, but note that latency-sensitive cache sharing across GPUs requires orchestration. In practice, we run a per-tenant cache instance that you can opt to have encrypted under your CMK.
- Model weights & artifacts: Private on-prem gives you full custody; Dedicated uses read-only stored weights on Redwood-managed storage encrypted at rest with CMK support.
- Network diagrams: I can produce an example VPC peering and private-control-plane diagram. It includes: private control-plane endpoints, SRE VPN jump host, and optional egress NAT gateways for pkg updates.

I'll bring the diagram and a short checklist (KMS endpoints, port list, audit export S3/BigQuery target) to the deep-dive. If you have an internal runbook for onboarding, please share the sections on network & key rotation so we can align.

-Neha
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
